# Independent signature and digest fixtures

These files are copied unchanged from the Apache-2.0-licensed
[Open Payments Elixir SDK at bf97d71](https://github.com/interledger/open-payments-elixir/tree/bf97d71b8b5e14f433c7ff1260eeeeab94901424/test/fixtures/signatures).
Their original source metadata and expected values are retained.

- `node-signatures.json`: upstream `node-signatures.json`, with nine Node.js
  v26.13.0 Ed25519 signatures. Six use `@interledger/http-signature-utils`2.0.3
  directly; three use its `http-message-signatures`1.0.8 dependency with exact
  content headers. The recorded bases were checked using Node's `crypto.verify`.
- `content-digests.json`: upstream `content-headers.json`, with eight SHA-512
  digest/byte-length cases generated by Node's `crypto.createHash` and Buffer.
  Its first case also matches [RFC9530 Appendix D](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9530.html#appendix-D).

The signatures use the publicly documented key from
[RFC8032 section7.1, test1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032.html#section-7.1),
with a fixed creation time of1618884473. All tokens are public test strings.
These keys must not be registered or used as application credentials.

Tests use the exact prepared URLs, body bytes, header values, component order
and signed parameters. They cover tenant paths, encoded queries, Unicode,
escaped key IDs, HTTP development URLs, IPv6, mixed header casing and explicit
empty bodies. The raw content cases are not all valid Open Payments payloads;
they test cryptographic framing independently of payload validation.

The verifier's clock is frozen for the old published signatures; separate tests
check age, expiry and future timestamps. Python's normal clock checks remain
enabled in the helper. No Node/Elixir installation or live provider is needed.
